text: The system shall allow a clinic employee to add a new pet owner by entering first name, last name, address, city and telephone number.
The system shall let an employee search for owners by last name; a partial last name matches and an empty search lists all owners.
The system shall show the owners that match a search in a paginated list of five owners per page.
When exactly one owner matches a search, the system shall go directly to that owner's details page.
When no owner matches a search, the system shall stay on the search page and show a 'not found' message.
The system shall display an owner's details: contact information, the owner's pets, and each pet's visit history.
The system shall allow an employee to update an existing owner's information.
The system shall allow an employee to add a new pet to an owner by entering the pet's name, birth date and type.
The system shall allow an employee to edit a pet's name, birth date and type.
The system shall require a pet name, a birth date and a type, and shall reject a pet name that the same owner already uses for another pet.
The system shall not accept a pet birth date that lies in the future.
The system shall allow an employee to schedule a visit for a pet by entering a date and a description.
The system shall list a pet's previous visits, with date and description, on the owner's details page.
The system shall list all veterinarians with their specialties in a paginated table.
The system shall also provide the list of veterinarians as a machine-readable resource (JSON or XML).
The system shall show a welcome page as the home page of the application.
When an unexpected error occurs, the system shall show a friendly error page instead of technical details.
The system shall present the user interface in the user's language, chosen from the browser locale or a language parameter, and support at least English, German and Spanish.
The system shall validate that an owner's telephone number consists of exactly ten digits and show a message in the user's language when it does not.
The system shall not accept an owner without a first name, last name, address and city.
The system shall cache the list of veterinarians so that repeated requests do not read the database again.
The system shall start with an in-memory database by default and also support MySQL and PostgreSQL through configuration.
The system shall protect against mass-assignment attacks by never binding the identifier fields of owners, pets and visits from a submitted form.
The system shall allow an owner to pay the invoice of a visit online by credit card.
The system shall send an email reminder to the owner 24 hours before a scheduled visit.
The system shall require employees to authenticate with a username and password before they can see or change owner data.
